title: CoreWeave Multi-Rack Rubin MLPerf Training Results
summary: CoreWeave delivers the first multi-rack NVIDIA Vera Rubin MLPerf Training results from a cloud provider, with faster performance across leading AI models.
body_markdown:
**LIVINGSTON, N.J. — November 16, 2026 —**[CoreWeave](https://www.coreweave.com/) , Inc. (Nasdaq: CRWV), The Essential Cloud for AI®, today announced its results in the MLPerf® Training v6.1 benchmark suite, including the first multi-rack results on[NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/data-center/vera-rubin-nvl72/) from any cloud provider. CoreWeave competed in the Closed division’s Available category, which compares systems apples-to-apples on the same reference model, using only hardware that customers can buy or rent today. It submitted results on NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 and[NVIDIA GB200 NVL72](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/data-center/gb200-nvl72/) systems across four models, from a single 72-GPU rack to 256 GPUs across multiple racks.


As frontier models grow larger and more complex, AI teams face a practical planning question: how much faster will a training run finish on the next generation of compute, and will that gain hold once the job spans multiple racks? A new GPU generation only pays off when the networking, orchestration, and operations around it keep every GPU productive at scale. MLPerf Training measures how long a system takes to reach a specified quality target. CoreWeave’s Training v6.1 submissions show how quickly Vera Rubin performance carries into a production multi-rack environment.


“New silicon is only as fast as the cloud it runs on,” said Chen Goldberg, EVP of product and engineering at CoreWeave. “Our MLPerf Training v6.1 results show what NVIDIA Vera Rubin can do when the full stack is built for it, from a single rack to multi-rack scale. We ran these benchmarks on the same production clusters our customers use to train frontier models, with CoreWeave Mission Control keeping the fleet healthy throughout.”


CoreWeave’s Training v6.1 submissions covered four model families. Key results include:


- **Multi-rack Vera Rubin delivered leading results with DeepSeek-V3 671B:** CoreWeave trained the 671-billion-parameter mixture-of-experts model to target quality in 17.65 minutes on 256 NVIDIA Rubin GPUs and[NVIDIA Spectrum-X Ethernet](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/networking/spectrumx/) networking across multiple racks. CoreWeave was the only cloud provider to submit results on this benchmark with NVIDIA Rubin.
- **2.7x faster than CoreWeave’s GB200 NVL72 submission:** At the same 256-GPU count, CoreWeave’s Vera Rubin result trained DeepSeek-V3 2.7x faster than its own GB200 NVL72 submission, a generation-over-generation improvement.¹
- **Fastest 72-GPU submission on Llama 3.1 8B:** On a single NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 rack, CoreWeave reached target quality in 7.16 minutes, the fastest 72-GPU submission. That is 1.9x faster than its 72-GPU GB200 NVL72 submission (13.70 minutes).¹
- **Strong results across model sizes on GB200 NVL72:** CoreWeave trained GPT-OSS 20B in 17.18 minutes on a single 72-GPU rack, and completed Qwen3.5 397B reinforcement learning in 22.78 minutes on 256 GPUs across multiple racks using NVIDIA NeMo-RL and NVIDIA[TensorRT](https://developer.nvidia.com/tensorrt) -LLM.


CoreWeave ran the benchmarks in the same production environment customers use. CoreWeave Mission Control provided fleet health monitoring and node and fleet lifecycle management, and a RoCE-based[NVIDIA Spectrum-X](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/networking/spectrumx/) Ethernet AI fabric with NVIDIA[ConnectX](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/networking/ethernet-adapters/) -9 SuperNICs connected the racks.


The MLPerf® training v6.1 results build on CoreWeave’s track record in independent evaluations, including its leading[MLPerf® Inference v6.1 results](https://www.coreweave.com/blog/coreweave-leads-cloud-providers-in-mlperf-r-inference-v6-1-performance-with-nvidia-blackwell-ultra) earlier this year and its position as the only AI cloud to earn the top[Platinum](https://www.coreweave.com/news/coreweave-becomes-the-only-provider-to-earn-semianalysis-platinum-clustermax-tm-rating-three-consecutive-times) ranking in SemiAnalysis ClusterMAX™ three times in a row.


Full results are available at[www.mlcommons.org](http://www.mlcommons.org/) .


*¹ Speedups are derived by CoreWeave from published MLCommons results, comparing CoreWeave’s Vera Rubin submissions with CoreWeave’s GB200 NVL72 submissions at the same GPU count.
